title: Investing in people, infrastructure, and meaningful collaboration is key for deep-sea biodiversity research and management in South Africa
content:
Abstract
After over a century of global research in the deep ocean, many nations continue to face barriers to developing and sustaining deep-sea research and management in their own waters. This prevents sound environmental management and limits nations’ potential to derive benefits from the deep sea. In this perspective paper, we draw on the experiences of established and early career researchers and managers in South Africa, to reflect on key obstacles limiting deep-sea biodiversity research and management in the country and propose potential solutions to strengthen the field. Challenges range from a lack of equal opportunity, cultural barriers, and poor retention of expertise, to limited financial support, low exposure to and perceived irrelevance of the deep sea, limited access to vessels and technology, and inequitable international standards and partnerships. Key enablers to support capacity development and increase equal opportunities in South African deep-sea biodiversity research and management include increased early exposure to the ocean and deep sea, financial and academic support, access to vessels and technology, and development of meaningful collaborations. We provide recommendations to increase capacity in five key theme areas: (i) exposure and training, (ii) mainstreaming, (iii) funding, (iv) research infrastructure, and (v) partnerships and research collaborations. These recommendations may inform researchers, funders, managers, decision-makers, industry stakeholders and international collaborators, and may be applicable to other developing nations facing similar challenges.
